CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient stepped off a curb while walking with his wife yesterday and landed on his left ankle incorrectly. He describes feeling the ankle extended and stretched rather than hearing a pop. Pain has been present for a couple of days, located on the outside of the ankle. He was able to walk home but with significant pain. He has been managing with ibuprofen and acetaminophen, elevation, ice, and weight-bearing avoidance. Pain level 8/10 without medication, decreasing to approximately 7/10 with medication. No previous substantial ankle injuries reported.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No substantial prior ankle injuries.

MEDICATIONS
Over-the-counter ibuprofen and acetaminophen.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works from home. Takes frequent walks with wife.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals stable but slightly elevated due to pain. Left ankle exam reveals ecchymosis and bruising over the lateral malleolus with swelling and edema. Tenderness to palpation on the lateral side with swollen soft tissue. No joint laxity appreciated. No bony tenderness to palpation of foot. Neurovascular exam: capillary refill brisk, less than 3 seconds. Strong dorsalis pedis pulses bilaterally. Motor and sensation intact bilaterally and symmetric.

RESULTS
X-ray of left ankle: No fracture or bony abnormalities.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left ankle sprain of the lateral ligament complex. Continue RICE protocol with elevation, compression, and ice. Prescribed air cast for ankle stabilization and crutches. Patient to remain off leg but begin walking as tolerated over next few days. Continue NSAIDs for pain and swelling reduction. Expect significant symptom improvement over 4-7 days. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks. Patient to return if symptoms worsen or questions arise.
